newsitem.title: GERMANY: Carnival spirit saps volumes in German share trade.
newsitem.headline: Carnival spirit saps volumes in German share trade.

text.p: Germany's IBIS DAX index ended sluggish trade slightly higher on Tuesday, with little volume around to forge any significant new gains, but dealers said the DAX index would likely clear the 3,200-point hurdle soon.

A half-day pre-Lent holiday in Frankfurt meant that volumes were thin and the IBIS DAX, which gauges electronic trade in 30 German blue-chips, ended the day at 3,191.45 points, up 5.73 points, or 0.18 percent.
Earlier the DAX index ended floor trade at 3,187.58 points, up 3.22 points or 0.10 percent.

"We expect we will pass the 3,200-point level in the next few days, but we need fresh liquidity to cross that hurdle. We have a lot of sectoral rotation going on at the moment because of the low volumes," said one trader.
The defining influence on trade in Frankfurt was once again the dollar, again at 1.67 marks, while an early rally to record highs for German debt futures also underpinned trade.

Dealers said one of the main gainers from dollar strength was the chemicals sector. BASF AG ended up 32 pfennigs at 63.18 marks, Bayer AG ended up 76 pfennigs at 66.92 marks and Hoechst AG ended up 65 pfennigs at 74.95 marks.

Drugs group Schering AG was strong after it reported a 46 percent increase in group net profit to 362 million marks in 1996 but fell in late IBIS trade to end off earlier highs down 10 pfennigs at 144.30 marks.

Shares in machine tool-maker Traub AG were suspended after bankruptcy proceedings were initiated, as it had previously indiated was likely following the failure of efforts to scale back debt with creditors.
